vignette: 67-year-old man with severe emphysema (ICD-10-CM J43.9) consistent with history and physical examination; BMI 26.4 kg/m2. He has been stable for 6 months on prednisone 5 mg daily. HRCT shows bilateral emphysema that the radiologist reads as severe and upper lobe predominant. Pre-rehabilitation pulmonary function: FEV1 27% predicted, DLCO 34% predicted, TLC 128% predicted and RV 215% predicted post-bronchodilator. Pre-rehabilitation room-air arterial blood gas at sea level: PCO2 44 mm Hg, PO2 63 mm Hg. Echocardiogram shows LVEF 60%; he is in sinus rhythm with no premature ventricular contractions on resting EKG and no angina. He completed an 8-week preoperative program of 18 sessions of 2.5 hours each, consistent with NETT, based on the treating physician's care plan after a comprehensive medical, psychosocial and nutritional evaluation and coordinated by the surgical facility; 7 postoperative sessions of 2 hours within 8 weeks after surgery are scheduled. Post-rehabilitation 6-minute walk is 265 m and he completed 3 minutes of unloaded pedaling before and after rehabilitation; maximal cycle ergometry workload after the program was 45 W. After rehabilitation, the pulmonologist, thoracic surgeon and anesthesiologist each documented approval for surgery. Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation are on file. He quit smoking 3 years ago; plasma cotinine is 3 ng/mL. Bilateral stapled lung volume reduction via video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery is planned at a hospital approved by Medicare as a lung transplantation hospital.
rationale_note: All criteria met; upper-lobe-predominant disease, so exercise capacity (45 W) does not matter.

vignette: 64-year-old woman with severe emphysema (ICD-10-CM J43.9) consistent with history and physical examination; BMI 29.8 kg/m2. She takes no systemic corticosteroids. HRCT shows bilateral severe emphysema that the radiologist reads as lower lobe predominant (non-upper lobe), with heterogeneous distribution. Pre-rehabilitation pulmonary function: FEV1 27% predicted, DLCO 34% predicted, TLC 128% predicted and RV 215% predicted post-bronchodilator. Pre-rehabilitation room-air arterial blood gas at sea level: PCO2 44 mm Hg, PO2 63 mm Hg. Echocardiogram shows LVEF 58%; she is in sinus rhythm with no premature ventricular contractions and no angina. She completed a 7-week preoperative program of 16 sessions of 2 hours each, consistent with NETT, based on the treating physician's care plan after a comprehensive medical, psychosocial and nutritional evaluation and coordinated by the surgical facility; 6 postoperative sessions of 2 hours within 8 weeks after surgery are scheduled. Post-rehabilitation 6-minute walk is 210 m and she completed 3 minutes of unloaded pedaling before and after rehabilitation; maximal cycle ergometry workload after the program (5 W/min ramp on 30% oxygen) was 25 W. After rehabilitation, the pulmonologist, thoracic surgeon and anesthesiologist each documented approval for surgery. Signed consents for screening and rehabilitation are on file. She quit smoking 18 months ago; plasma cotinine is 2 ng/mL. Bilateral stapled lung volume reduction via median sternotomy is planned at a hospital certified by the Joint Commission under the LVRS Disease Specific Care Certification Program.
rationale_note: Boundary: woman with non-upper-lobe emphysema and maximal workload exactly 25 W (low exercise capacity).
